45	CASE OD2-DEV-INCOMPLETE: Missed appointments after the scheduler change at Corrie Lane Outpatient Centre

47	Setting: Corrie Lane Outpatient Centre is one of two outpatient sites run by Hollins Vale Hospitals, a fictional regional hospital group. 48

50	
51	INITIAL EVIDENCE
52	E1 [stage S1] Email from Mairead Tolland, Director of Outpatient Operations, 9 Sept 2026 (leadership-account): Our did-not-attend (DNA) rate at Corrie Lane has gone from about 8% to over 13% since Tidewell went live on 3 March. The board wants an explanation and a fix by November. My view: the front desk stopped the day-before confirmation calls when the old system's printed call sheets went, and nobody told me. I'd like you to confirm that so I can deal with it through the team leads. Owen thinks it's partly the March cuts to the route 14 bus and partly that Tidewell 'counts differently'. 53	E2 [stage S1] Outpatient performance dashboard, Corrie Lane, extract 8 Sept 2026 (system-record): Monthly DNA rate (DNAs divided by appointments still booked on the day). Footnote 2: according to the analytics team, month-to-month differences under 1 percentage point are normal variation at this volume.
54	E3 [stage S1] Change record CR-2026-0117, Tidewell go-live, Corrie Lane (change-record): Go-live 3 March 2026. All three specialties (orthopaedics, dermatology, endocrinology) switched over on the same day. Configuration: (1) Messaging. The legacy system sent one SMS 48 hours before each appointment. Tidewell sends a confirmation SMS at booking plus one reminder SMS at a fixed offset, set to 7 days (the vendor default). Tidewell allows one reminder offset per session template, and the vendor can change the offset for any template within two working days. (2) Booking. New and follow-up templates open 16 weeks ahead (legacy: 6 weeks). Follow-ups are booked at checkout instead of going on the recall list. (3) Outcome codes. The legacy code 'Arrived late – not seen' is mapped to Tidewell 'DNA'. Rollback: legacy system decommissioned 30 April.
55	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Bisi Adeyemi-Clarke, front-desk team lead, 12 Sept 2026 (staff-account): BA-C: 'We never stopped the calls. 56	E5 [stage S1] Patient Advice desk log, Corrie Lane, scheduling-related entries May–Aug 2026 (customer-account): Extracts (4 of 23 scheduling-related entries): (a) 'Used to get a text two days before. Now I get one a week before, and by the day I'd forgotten.' (b) 'Got a text the day I booked and one a week before, nothing nearer the time. Missed my endocrine review.' (c) 'Why are you texting me a week early? I nearly came on the wrong day.' (d) 'Was given an August date back in April. My shifts changed in the meantime and I couldn't get through on the phone to move it.' The other 19 entries: phone waiting times (11), car parking (5), other (3).
57	E6 [stage S1] Note from Owen Faraday, Clinic Manager, Corrie Lane, 10 Sept 2026 (manager-account): Honestly, I think a good chunk of this is Tidewell counting differently. The old system had a separate 'arrived late – not seen' code, and the migration lumped all of that into DNA. Until the data people sort out March and April, I'd suggest we stop sending the DNA figure to the board, because it makes us look worse than we are. The other thing is the bus. 3	Source: Clinical audit team (lead: R. Gilchrist) (independent-observation)
4	
5	Random sample of 200 Tidewell appointments coded DNA in May–June, checked against clinician notes, kiosk check-in logs and same-day pathology or imaging requests. 193 (96.5%): no evidence of attendance. 4 (2.0%): arrived late and not seen (the legacy system would have coded these 'late – not seen'). 3 (1.5%): attended and seen, outcome keyed wrongly. Audit conclusion: miscoded records make up about 3.5% of DNA codes, roughly 0.5 percentage points of the 13.4% rate. Miscoding does not explain a rise of the size reported.

input.brief:
The rise in missed appointments looks real and is tied to the Tidewell change. It is not a bus problem, a seasonal effect or a counting artefact. Eastgate, which kept the old system, stayed at about 8% and shares the bus route. Corrie Lane was about 8% in the same months a year earlier. A clinical audit found miscoded records add only about 0.5 points to the rate. The front-desk calls were only ever for the minor-procedures list. Nothing shows they stopped, so written warnings would punish the wrong people. Hiding the figure from the board would also be wrong.

Two changes took effect on the same day. Reminders moved from 48 hours to 7 days before the appointment. Booking lead time went from a median of about 19 days to about 52. The data can't separate them. Every template and every specialty changed together, and we can't link outcomes to lead time. I'm unsure which is the larger driver, and both may contribute.

Next step: run the 8-week test with a 48-hour reminder on a random half of templates. The vendor can make that change within two working days. Order the appointment-level extract now. Report the DNA rate to the board with this explanation. Don't revert the booking horizon or switch every template yet.
